question: Does the MUTCD apply to roadways inside a shopping center that are open to public travel, and does it apply to the parking spaces and driving aisles within the parking area?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Yes, the MUTCD applies to roadways within shopping centers that are open to public travel without full-time access restrictions — these are explicitly named as "site roadways open to public travel." However, the MUTCD does not apply to the parking areas themselves, including the driving aisles within those parking areas, regardless of whether they are publicly or privately owned. Standards (mandatory): - "In accordance with 23 CFR 655.603(a), the MUTCD shall apply to... Streets and roadways on sites that are off the public right-of-way that are open to public travel without full-time access restrictions. Examples include roadways within shopping centers, office parks, airports, sports arenas, other similar business and/or recreation facilities... The above-described examples of streets and roadways are referred to in this Manual as site roadways open to public travel." - "The MUTCD shall not apply to the following types of facilities: ... C. Parking areas, including the driving aisles within those parking areas, that are either publicly or privately owned." Guidance (recommended): - Before requesting permission to experiment with a new device or application, an owner of a site roadway open to public travel should first check for any laws, regulations, and/or directives covering the application of the MUTCD that might apply. Citations: - Section 1B.01 Standard §2 (p.4) - Section 1B.01 Standard §3 (p.4) - Section 1A.01 Support §5 (p.1) - Section 1B.05 Guidance §7 (p.7)
gold_answer: It applies to the shopping-center site roadways that are open to public travel without full-time access restrictions. It does not apply to the parking area itself, including its driving aisles.
